items.stem: Which Gmail feature automatically applies a label and skips the inbox for matching incoming mail?

options.rationale: Correct: filters can label, archive and route incoming messages automatically.
A signature is appended text, not a sorting rule.
Stars are manual markers, not automatic rules.

items.explanation: Correct: filters can label, archive and route incoming messages automatically.

items.stem: You must email three external vendors without exposing their addresses to each other. Which field do you use?

options.rationale: Correct: Bcc keeps recipients' addresses hidden from one another.
To exposes all addresses to everyone.
Cc also exposes addresses to all recipients.
The subject line does not control address visibility.

items.explanation: Correct: Bcc keeps recipients' addresses hidden from one another.

items.stem: Which TWO signals should raise suspicion of a phishing email? (Select TWO.)

options.text: An urgent request to click a link and verify credentials
options.rationale: Correct: urgency plus credential requests is a classic phishing pattern.

options.text: A sender address that mimics but does not match the real domain
options.rationale: Correct: look-alike domains are a common spoofing tactic.

options.text: A message from a colleague you expected
options.rationale: Expected, verifiable mail is not inherently suspicious.

options.text: A plain-text internal newsletter you subscribed to
options.rationale: A subscribed newsletter is not a phishing signal.

items.explanation: Correct: urgency with credential requests and look-alike sender domains are both phishing signals.
